blocks.caption: The Hummingbird, queen of the hover

blocks.text: There are two ways to fly, and a good flyer learns both. One is for building and looking, the other for crossing the world.

Entered with a very fast double tap of jump in the air, or Left Alt from travel flight. You hang in the air like a builder in creative mode, and move with W, A, S, D, jump and sneak. Each pair hovers at its own speed and rhythm.

The Stability stat decides how calm you are. At 0 each beat bobs you up and down by more than half a block and makes you drift; at 10 you are still as stone. Short taps start slowly, so you can nudge yourself a block at a time.
Hovering drains 2.5 stamina per second. At zero you simply fall, with your rescue jumps left. Touch the ground without holding jump and you land.

Entered with Left Alt in the air, or the charged take-off on the ground. Hold sprint to beat, let go to glide. Speed comes in a sawtooth: a push at each beat, a slow fade between them, up to the cruise speed of your pair.
Gliding costs nothing and even gives back 3 stamina per second. Climbing trades speed for height; diving trades height for speed.
Point your nose down and gravity pulls you faster than any beat. With wings open, a vertical dive tops out at 120 m/s.

Dive at least 15 degrees nose down, already faster than cruise speed, and hold sprint: you fold your wings like a stooping falcon. The air barely holds you then, up to 220 m/s. Pull up and the extra speed bleeds away back to cruise.

The brake slows you by twice your Acceleration each second, so powerful wings stop hard and weak ones barely at all. In a steep dive, the brake fights gravity: weak wings must pull up early. Below a crawl, a last beat stops you and you fall into a hover.

Fly too slowly without braking, by climbing too long for instance, and your wings stall: no more lift, and you drop. Dive to win back speed and the wings bite the air again. The Lift stat sets how slow you can go before stalling.

In travel flight, touching the ground ends your flight. What hurts is the speed you hit it with, straight into the surface: below 10 m/s nothing happens, above it each m/s costs 0.5 damage. A fast, grazing landing is survivable; a straight dive into the ground is not. Walls count too.
You cannot fly in water or lava, while riding, or while sleeping.
